title: Officers 'acted appropriately' in police shooting that killed London man, report says
subtitle: Samuel Maloney, 35, was fatally shot by police in his Old South home
article: An internal report released Friday says London police officers acted appropriately during a police shooting that killed a London man while officers executed a search warrant at his Old South home in December, 2016.

The report by the professional standards branch of the London Police Services (LPS) makes findings similar to a Special Investigations Unit (SIU) report into the shooting released in June 2018. That report found that London police officers did not break the law when they shot Samuel Maloney. The report stated responding officers only fired on Maloney after he shot an officer with a crossbow after they had entered his home.

On the morning of December 23, 2016, eleven emergency response unit (ERU) officers used a ram to enter Maloney's home on Duchess Avenue. Police were investigating complaints that Maloney had posted anti-Semitic materials to the website of a local cinema.
Maloney's wife and two young children were in the house when police shot and killed the 35-year-old man shortly after they entered the home.

The report says police encountered Maloney in the front computer room of the house and an officer was shot "in the chest/abdominal area with a crossbow without warning." An officer shot Maloney in the chest, hitting him once in the shoulder. The report says the officer "retreated and began communications with other members of the ERU as well as Mr. Maloney, attempting to de-escalate the situation and convince him to come out with his hands empty."
The report says Maloney ignored police commands. It also says Maloney held a hatchet above his head and ran to the "rear bedroom area" of the house while screaming.
A second officer, positioned near the rear bedroom, then shot Maloney in the chest.
Maloney fell at the bedroom doorway and was shot again by a third officer, striking him in the head. He was pronounced dead at the scene.
The LPS report released Friday repeats comments from SIU director Tony Loparco: that all three officers who shot Maloney that morning "were in the lawful execution of their duties."
The report also includes a review of police actions by Sgt. Andrew Bakker, the designated use-of-force instructor with London police.
"It is my respectful opinion that these officers acted appropriately in these circumstances as outlined within the SIU report," Bakker wrote.
A coroner's inquest into the shooting will be held, but a date has not yet been set.
Maloney's wife is also suing police.
